terms.label: APR
terms.definition: The yearly cost of borrowing, as a percentage. A card at 24% APR charges about 2% of the balance every month.

terms.label: minimum payment
terms.definition: The smallest amount a lender will accept this month. Paying it keeps the account in good standing; it does not mean the balance is going down much.

terms.label: payoff projection
terms.definition: How long the balance takes to reach zero at the payment you are making. If the payment does not cover the monthly interest, there is no answer.

terms.label: principal
terms.definition: The amount borrowed, separate from the interest charged on it.

terms.label: amortization
terms.definition: Paying a loan off in level instalments. Early payments are mostly interest; later ones are mostly principal.

terms.label: grace period
terms.definition: If a card statement is paid in full, new purchases accrue no interest. Carry a balance once and the grace period ends until it is cleared again.

terms.label: utilization
terms.definition: The share of your available credit you are using. It is one of the five inputs to a credit score.

terms.label: credit score
terms.definition: A 300-850 number lenders use to price a loan. It does not exist until you have had a credit line open for about six months.

terms.label: net worth
terms.definition: Everything you own minus everything you owe. It can be negative.

terms.label: emergency fund
terms.definition: Cash set aside for the unplanned. Usually measured in months of expenses it would cover.

terms.label: dividend
terms.definition: A share of profit paid to shareholders, usually quarterly. It is taxed in the year you receive it, whether or not you spend it.

terms.label: auto-reinvest
terms.definition: Using dividends to buy more shares automatically. The tax is still owed, even though no cash arrived.

terms.label: cost basis
terms.definition: What you paid for shares. The gain that gets taxed is the sale price minus this.

terms.label: capital gain
terms.definition: The profit on selling an asset for more than you paid. Held under a year it is taxed as ordinary income; held a year or more, at a lower rate.

terms.label: tax lot
terms.definition: One purchase of shares, with its own price and date. Sales use the oldest lot first.

terms.label: marginal rate
terms.definition: The rate charged on your next dollar of income — not on all of it.

terms.label: withholding
terms.definition: Tax taken from a paycheque before you see it. Side income and investment income are not withheld, which is where a year-end bill comes from.

terms.label: nominal
terms.definition: A figure before adjusting for inflation. A 3% raise in a 4% inflation year is a nominal rise and a real fall.

terms.label: real terms
terms.definition: A figure adjusted for inflation, so amounts from different years can be compared.

terms.label: CPI
terms.definition: An index of what a basket of goods costs. Used here to restate past amounts in today's money.

terms.label: underwater
terms.definition: Owing more on a loan than the thing it bought is worth.

terms.label: depreciation
terms.definition: The loss of value over time. A new car loses about 12% the moment it is driven away.

terms.label: employer match
terms.definition: Money an employer adds to your retirement account when you contribute. Contributing less than the match leaves it unclaimed.

terms.label: volatility
terms.definition: How much a price moves around. High volatility drags the typical outcome below the average one.

terms.label: diversification
terms.definition: Holding several unrelated things so one of them going wrong does not decide everything.

terms.label: Buy Now Pay Later
terms.definition: Four instalments over six weeks, interest-free. It is a debt from the moment of purchase and appears on the balance sheet as one.
